newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.9 pct in Aug -- Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.9 pct in Aug -- Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.9 percent in August versus July based on sales for the first three weeks of fiscal August, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.

The index rose 6.8 percent when compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales also rose 6.2 percent in the week ended August 24 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
"(Sales) slowed down a bit from that very unusual spurt of activity we got in the first week of August," said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Lynch, Jones & Ryan.
Although retailers started the month above-plan, sales in last week generally were near or below projected levels, Eilenberg said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
"The majority (of stores) will achieve their objectives," he said. "But at least two big companies said they would not meet their expectations."
Demand for back-to-school items bolstered sales somewhat and should continue to do so in September, Eilenberg said.
"Going forward, it should be a good fall season, since the economy's holding up," he said.
